title: Talent radar - 1:1 prep and follow-ups
body:
Quick scratchpad for 1:1 with A. (weekly headcount + interview loop cleanup).

Context:
- sprint of hiring: closing 4 IC roles this quarter, 2 managers open. Pressure on SRE/Serving team for Q2 capacity.
- hiring velocity dip last 3 weeks; need to unblock loop assignment and interview availability.

Meeting goals (top 3):
1) Confirm hiring commits for Eng-Serving: 3 IC (backend, inference infra, quantitative infra) + 1 TPM.
2) Reassign interview loops to reduce single-point-of-failure interviewers (Maya currently on 7 loops).
3) Agree next steps for candidate debrief turnaround SLA (target: 48h).

Agenda (30min):
- 0-5m: quick sync on hiring health (numbers)
- 5-12m: priority roles and blockers (who owns writing JD updates)
- 12-20m: interview loops (who covers, calibrations, rubric gaps)
- 20-27m: debrief -> action owners and timeline
- 27-30m: quick retrospective on last hire (what sped up / slowed down)

Headcount snapshot (numbers to confirm in meeting):
- Q2 hiring plan (committed): 6 net new eng seats (2 for serving runtime, 1 for infra, 1 for console, 2 TBD)
- Open reqs: REC-4091 (Backend IC), REC-4123 (Inference infra IC), REC-4150 (TPM), REC-4177 (SRE IC), REC-4199 (Manager, Console)
- Offers out: 1 (Backend IC) — candidate expecting response by 3/15

Interview loop notes / proposed reassignments:
- Current pain: interviewers with >5 active loops: Maya L (7), Raj P (6), Samir K (5) -> burn risk.
- Proposed: move two loops off Maya to wider panel (add Mila, Arjun as 2nd/3rd interviewers).
- Need to schedule a 30m calibration session (rubric + 'design for production' diffs) before next loop batch. Owner: Raj (due 3/18).

Candidate debrief template (quick, to reduce friction):
- Candidate: [name] | Role: [req] | Stage: [onsite / loop]
- Rating summary (1-5): technical / product sense / communication / org fit
- Y/N hire? + reasons and open questions
- Must-have concerns (list)
- Suggested next step (hold / offer / nope / more interviews)
- PRS: who to follow up (recruiter) and target timeline

Actions (explicit, short):
- Neha: update REC-4123 JD with specific infra benchmarks + internal benchmark links (due 3/11) [DONE]
- Raj: schedule rubric calibration 30m with interviewer pool (due 3/18)
- Maya: hand off two loops (REC-4150, REC-4177) to Mila + Arjun; include context doc (due 3/13)
- Recruiter (Lina): pump passive candidate list for Manager, Console by 3/20 and share shortlist
- Hiring committee: adopt 48h debrief SLA; note exceptions and escalate reasons in thread

Risks / open questions (notes-to-self):
- If offers start getting declined -> what's the fallback? extra sign-on pool? hire-faster comp band increase? need headcount finance pre-approval.
- Interviewer fatigue: consider 1-2 week 'cooldown' after >6 loops in a month. Is that feasible? Discuss with SRE and Eng managers.
- Private deployment customers demand experienced infra hire — consider prioritizing REC-4123 over Console manager.

Notes to self (random scribbles):
- Keep debrief short; force binary decision. Add quick checkboxes in Greenhouse for debrief items.
- Prep one-pager for A before 1:1: include numbers + 1 suggested reprioritization (swap Console manager to Q3, accelerate infra IC to Q2).
- Bring finance note: what happens if we accelerate offers (impact on quarterly spend) -> ask K.

Follow-ups to add to calendar:
- 15m pre-read sent to A: headcount snapshot + proposed loop reassignment (send today)
- 30m rubric calibration (invite list: Maya, Raj, Samir, Mila, Arjun)
- Retro on last closed hire: 20m (capture 3 lessons)

Unresolved / quick TODOs after meeting:
- Add rescue signal in case candidate offers stall (who signs off on increased band?)
- Build a tiny dashboard: open reqs by time-in-loop, average debrief latency (aim <48h). Ask Observability to sketch metrics (Raj to connect).

Quick capture of language to use in 1:1: 
- "I want us to be aggressive on infra hires this quarter; the backlog risk is material."
- "Short debriefs = faster cycles. If we need more info, we can trigger a follow-up rather than hold decisions."
